title: Can anyone rebuild the hardware?
title_zh: 這些硬體，別人做得出來嗎？
lede: Of 20 instruments built by the 2026 Best Hardware, Best Measurement and Best Alternative Platform cohorts, 6 publish enough for a stranger in another country to rebuild them. Nine publish no geometry file at all. One has ever been used by someone outside the team that built it.
lede_zh: 2026 年 Best Hardware、Best Measurement 與 Best Alternative Platform 這三組隊伍總共做出 20 台儀器，其中只有 6 台公開的資料足以讓另一個國家的陌生人重建出來。有 9 台完全沒有釋出任何幾何檔案。而真正被原團隊以外的人用過的，只有 1 台。
body:
**Six of twenty.** That is how many award-winning iGEM 2026 instruments a stranger could actually rebuild: NCKU-Tainan's CAPTURE-Screen fluorescence reader, Lambert-GA's Vapor-X vacuum dryer, UNILausanne's C.L.A.W. LAMP incubator, Hongwen School's BrewXOS Fermenter Mini, TU Darmstadt's anaerobic chamber trio, and GEMS-Taiwan's four ReLEAF devices. Two more — Princeton's gyroid biofilter and CalPolySLO's emulsification washboard — are single printed parts where an STL plus print settings is the whole deliverable, which takes the generous count to eight. Everything else is missing at least one thing a second builder cannot do without.

The sister analysis of software found that every repository was populated, because iGEM mandates a GitLab deposit, and that the thing separating live tools from dead ones was a hosting decision. Hardware has no such floor. **There is no `2026/hardware` group on gitlab.igem.org at all** — the API returns 404 for it while `2026/software` returns a group called Software. Every hardware release in this cohort is improvised: a sub-project filed under `/software/`, a personal GitHub account, an Onshape link, a Google Drive folder, or loose files on the wiki's asset store. Nothing in the competition ever asks a hardware team to press Export.

And pressing Export is exactly the separating habit. The teams you cannot rebuild from are not lazy and their CAD is not missing — it is visibly, beautifully *rendered*. Cornell's Best Hardware winner has an exploded view of the Arachne electrospinner and a bill of materials so good it names Analog Technologies' AHV24V30KVR5MAW at $419.00 across 40 priced line items totalling $1,213.35 — and then says, in the present tense of a page that will not change again, "we plan to provide a bill of materials, CAD files, circuit diagrams, assembly documentation, and an operation manual." Two PDFs went up; no CAD file, no schematic file and no firmware ever did. CAU-China's OptiX phone spectrometer has an interactive exploded CAD view with numbered, clickable components and the most careful calibration chain in the whole cohort — and not one downloadable file, not one priced part, on a $12–30 instrument whose entire pitch is that anyone can have one. NU Boston published CAD drawings with dimensions and tolerances as figures. UBC-Vancouver published `.glb` meshes, a render format. In every one of these cases the model exists; it simply never left the design tool in a format anyone else can open.

The six that cleared the bar all did one unglamorous thing: they wrote the build as a document with files attached, not a page with pictures attached. NCKU-Tainan's MIT-licensed repo holds 225 files — 75 STEP exports, 59 STLs, the parametric CadQuery Python they were generated from, an ESP32 sketch with its own AS7341 driver, a bill-of-materials CSV and a 12-step assembly order that a second builder checked against the real machine. Its costing is the most honest number in the census: US$160.62 for the printed build, broken down to the print-shop receipt, with the line "an estimate, not an account" and the NT$31.68/US$1 rate it was converted at. Lambert-GA shipped Gerbers, a drill file, a JLCPCB pick-and-place CSV and a BOM keyed to LCSC part numbers, so the board can be ordered without a human in the loop. UNILausanne's C.L.A.W. costs under CHF 10, ships five STLs and a 3.8 MB manual, and includes the calibration that matters: a thermometer in the tube bore reads about 10 °C above the display, so the thermostat is set to 52.5 °C, preheated ten minutes, and holds 62.7 ± 1.2 °C over 30 minutes across three runs.

Two links fail the moment you check them rather than read them. Toronto's bioreactor page points at a Google Drive folder called "Bioreactor CAD Files"; opened signed-out it shows the folder name, no files, and a prompt to sign in — so the CAD for a $204 CAD bioreactor is, in practice, unavailable, while the firmware beside it is public and Apache-2.0. HongKong-JSS does the opposite: its Onshape document loads for anyone, 28 parts and a full feature tree, while `github.com/hkjssplkchc2026/mercurysense` — the firmware, the C12880 spectrometer driver and the acquisition instructions, as named on their own wiki — returns 404, and that GitHub account has no public repositories at all. Costs deserve the same scepticism. NU Boston's FLARE leads with "as low as $300 vs $10,000", then publishes two bills of materials totalling $499.80 and $344.18, **neither of which contains the Raspberry Pi 5 or the Arduino that run the instrument**. By contrast HongKong-JSS states plainly that its USD 357 build missed the USD 40 its stakeholders asked for, and TU Darmstadt records that the oxygen sensor is 83% of its €114.60 monitor.

Outside use is bleaker than it was for software. Across every hardware repository checked the fork count is zero and the star count is zero, with one exception: Bist-China's seven STLs on GitHub have two stars — and no licence file, so nobody may legally reuse them. The single genuine case of a device leaving its makers is Lambert-GA's, and it is a high-school team: they shipped Vapor-X to the Biochemical Genetics Laboratory at the University of Alabama at Birmingham, where John Moore measured 38 of 43 compounds recovered within 5% of undried controls, and to the Styczynski Lab at Georgia Tech, which checked GFP fluorescence after drying DNA and lysates. Both labs' raw data are downloadable. **One team in twenty asked an outsider to use the thing, and the one that did was the one with Gerbers.**
body_zh:
**二十台裡有六台。** 這是 2026 年得獎儀器中，陌生人真的做得出來的數量：NCKU-Tainan 的 CAPTURE-Screen 螢光判讀儀、Lambert-GA 的 Vapor-X 真空乾燥機、UNILausanne 的 C.L.A.W. LAMP 恆溫器、Hongwen School 的 BrewXOS Fermenter Mini、TU Darmstadt 的三件厭氧套件，以及 GEMS-Taiwan 的四台 ReLEAF 裝置。另有兩件——Princeton 的 gyroid 生物濾材與 CalPolySLO 的乳化搓板——本身就是單一列印件，一個 STL 加上列印參數就是全部交付物，寬鬆算來可以湊到八台。其餘每一台，都至少缺了第二個製作者非有不可的某樣東西。

軟體那篇姊妹分析發現：每一個儲存庫都有實質內容，因為 iGEM 強制要求把原始碼存進 GitLab；真正決定工具生死的，是一個關於架站的決定。硬體沒有這道底線。**gitlab.igem.org 上根本沒有 `2026/hardware` 這個群組**——API 對它回 404，而 `2026/software` 回的是一個名為 Software 的群組。這批隊伍的硬體釋出全是各自想辦法：掛在 `/software/` 底下的子專案、個人 GitHub 帳號、一條 Onshape 連結、一個 Google Drive 資料夾，或是散落在 wiki 靜態檔案區的零散檔案。整場比賽從來沒有任何一個環節，要求硬體隊伍按下「匯出」。

而「按下匯出」正是那個分水嶺習慣。那些你重建不了的隊伍，並不是偷懶，他們的 CAD 也沒有不見——而是被漂漂亮亮地「算圖」成了圖片。Cornell 這支 Best Hardware 冠軍隊，有一張 Arachne 靜電紡絲機的爆炸圖，還有一份好到會寫出 Analog Technologies AHV24V30KVR5MAW、單價 $419.00 的物料清單，40 個逐項報價的品項合計 $1,213.35——然後，在一個不會再更動的頁面上，用現在式寫著：「我們計畫提供物料清單、CAD 檔案、電路圖、組裝文件與操作手冊。」最後上傳的是兩份 PDF；沒有任何一個 CAD 檔、電路圖檔或韌體。CAU-China 的 OptiX 手機光譜儀有一張可點選、元件逐一編號的互動式爆炸 CAD 視圖，校正鏈也是整批隊伍中做得最細的——卻連一個可下載的檔案、一項標價的零件都沒有，而這台儀器的全部訴求，就是 $12 到 $30、人人都能有一台。NU Boston 把標注尺寸與公差的 CAD 圖當成插圖發表。UBC-Vancouver 發表的是 `.glb`，一種算圖用的格式。上述每一個案例，模型都存在；它只是從來沒有以別人打得開的格式離開過設計軟體。

過關的那六支，都做了同一件不起眼的事：他們把製作過程寫成一份附帶檔案的文件，而不是一個附帶圖片的網頁。NCKU-Tainan 以 MIT 授權的儲存庫裡有 225 個檔案——75 個 STEP 匯出檔、59 個 STL、生成這些檔案的參數化 CadQuery Python、一支自帶 AS7341 驅動程式的 ESP32 韌體、一份物料清單 CSV，以及一份由第二位製作者對照實機核對過的 12 步組裝順序。它的成本估算是這份普查中最誠實的數字：3D 列印版 US$160.62，拆到列印店的收據，並附上「這是估算，不是帳目」這句話，以及換算所用的 NT$31.68 兌 US$1 匯率。Lambert-GA 釋出了 Gerber 檔、鑽孔檔、JLCPCB 貼片座標 CSV，以及一份以 LCSC 料號編寫的物料清單，所以這塊板子可以在沒有人介入的情況下直接下單。UNILausanne 的 C.L.A.W. 成本不到 CHF 10，附五個 STL 與一份 3.8 MB 的手冊，而且寫進了真正關鍵的校正：把溫度計直接插進試管孔，讀到的溫度比面板顯示高約 10 °C，所以恆溫器設在 52.5 °C、預熱十分鐘，三次獨立測試中 30 分鐘內維持在 62.7 ± 1.2 °C。

有兩條連結，只要去點它、而不是去讀它，就當場失效。Toronto 的生物反應器頁面指向一個名為「Bioreactor CAD Files」的 Google Drive 資料夾；未登入開啟時只看得到資料夾名稱、沒有任何檔案，還跳出要你登入的提示——所以這台 204 加幣生物反應器的 CAD，實際上拿不到，而旁邊的韌體卻是公開的 Apache-2.0。HongKong-JSS 則剛好相反：它的 Onshape 文件任何人都開得起來，28 個零件、完整特徵樹俱在，但他們自己 wiki 上寫明收著韌體、C12880 光譜儀驅動程式與擷取說明的 `github.com/hkjssplkchc2026/mercurysense` 回應 404，而且那個 GitHub 帳號底下一個公開儲存庫也沒有。成本同樣值得用一樣的懷疑去看。NU Boston 的 FLARE 以「低至 $300，相對於 $10,000」開場，接著公開了兩份物料清單，合計分別是 $499.80 與 $344.18，**而兩份都沒有放進驅動這台儀器的 Raspberry Pi 5 或 Arduino**。相對地，HongKong-JSS 直白寫出他們 USD 357 的製作成本沒有達到利害關係人要求的 USD 40，TU Darmstadt 也記下氧氣感測器佔了那台 €114.60 監測器的 83%。

至於外部使用，情況比軟體那邊更慘。所有被檢查過的硬體儲存庫，分支數都是零、星星數也都是零，只有一個例外：Bist-China 放在 GitHub 上的七個 STL 有兩顆星——卻沒有授權條款檔案，所以沒有人可以合法地拿去用。唯一一個儀器真正離開製作者手中的案例來自 Lambert-GA，而且是一支高中隊伍：他們把 Vapor-X 寄到 University of Alabama at Birmingham 的 Biochemical Genetics Laboratory，由 John Moore 量得 43 個化合物中有 38 個的回收率落在未乾燥對照組的 5% 以內；也寄到 Georgia Tech 的 Styczynski Lab，由他們檢查 DNA 與細胞裂解液乾燥後的 GFP 螢光。兩間實驗室的原始資料都可以下載。**二十支隊伍中只有一支請外人實際用過自己的東西，而做到這件事的，正是那支連 Gerber 檔都備齊的隊伍。**

cards.title: Vapor-X — the only device an outsider has used
cards.title_zh: Vapor-X——唯一有外人用過的裝置
cards.body: Lambert-GA's $80.07 vacuum dryer (a Mason jar, a 12 V pump, a polyimide heater and a Raspberry Pi Pico W on a custom PCB) is the only instrument in this cohort with third-party evidence. The team shipped it to the Biochemical Genetics Laboratory at the University of Alabama at Birmingham, where John Moore recovered 38 of 43 measured compounds within 5% of undried controls, and to the Styczynski Lab at Georgia Tech for GFP fluorescence after drying. The release matches: three STLs, a complete Gerber and drill set, a JLCPCB pick-and-place CSV, a BOM keyed to LCSC part numbers, MicroPython firmware under Apache-2.0, and an 8.5 MB construction manual. It is the only release here that a board house could execute without a human reading the wiki.
cards.body_zh: Lambert-GA 這台 $80.07 的真空乾燥機（一只梅森罐、一顆 12 V 真空幫浦、一片聚醯亞胺加熱片，以及一塊自製 PCB 上的 Raspberry Pi Pico W），是這批隊伍中唯一有第三方證據的儀器。團隊把它寄到 University of Alabama at Birmingham 的 Biochemical Genetics Laboratory，由 John Moore 測得 43 個化合物中有 38 個回收率落在未乾燥對照組的 5% 以內；也寄到 Georgia Tech 的 Styczynski Lab，檢查乾燥後的 GFP 螢光。釋出的內容也相稱：三個 STL、一整套 Gerber 與鑽孔檔、一份 JLCPCB 貼片座標 CSV、一份以 LCSC 料號編寫的物料清單、以 Apache-2.0 授權的 MicroPython 韌體，以及一份 8.5 MB 的製作手冊。這是此處唯一一份板廠不必有人去讀 wiki 就能直接施工的釋出。

cards.title: NCKU-Tainan shipped the source, not just the export
cards.title_zh: NCKU-Tainan 釋出的是原始檔，不只是匯出檔
cards.body: 225 files under MIT: 75 STEP assemblies, 59 STLs covering 66 printed pieces across two builds, and the parametric CadQuery Python the geometry was generated from — so another team can change a dimension rather than reprint yours. Alongside it sit an ESP32 sketch with its own AS7341 driver, a bill-of-materials CSV, a bench schematic with measured values, and working sensor settings (AGAIN 512x, ATIME 255, ASTEP 280). The costing is itemised by basis — print-shop receipts, costing sheet, distributor list prices — totals US$160.62 for the printed build and US$53.70 for the laser-cut one, and is labelled "an estimate, not an account". They also publish what failed: the laser-cut build could not tell the AHL sensor strain from cells without sfGFP.
cards.body_zh: 以 MIT 授權釋出的 225 個檔案：75 個 STEP 組件、涵蓋兩個版本共 66 個列印件的 59 個 STL，以及生成這些幾何的參數化 CadQuery Python——所以別的隊伍可以改尺寸，而不是只能照著你的檔案重印。旁邊還放著一支自帶 AS7341 驅動程式的 ESP32 韌體、一份物料清單 CSV、一張標有實測值的電路圖，以及可用的感測器設定（AGAIN 512x、ATIME 255、ASTEP 280）。成本逐項標明依據——列印店收據、自家成本表、經銷商牌價——3D 列印版合計 US$160.62、雷射切割版 US$53.70，並註明「這是估算，不是帳目」。他們也把失敗寫出來：雷射切割版分不出 AHL 感測菌株與不帶 sfGFP 的細胞。

cards.kicker: The gap between page and file
cards.kicker_zh: 頁面與檔案之間的落差
cards.title: The Best Hardware winner published no CAD at all
cards.title_zh: Best Hardware 冠軍隊一個 CAD 檔都沒有釋出
cards.body: Cornell's Arachne electrospinner won Best Hardware (Undergraduate) with a genuinely excellent bill of materials — 40 priced line items in three groups, from the $419.00 Analog Technologies AHV24V30KVR5MAW 30 kV supply to $0.08 M5 screws, subtotals $681.76 / $416.87 / $114.72, total $1,213.35 — and a fabrication-and-assembly guide and safety manual that both download. What never appeared is the geometry: no STL, no STEP, no circuit schematic file and no ESP32 firmware anywhere on the hardware, circuitry, encasement or contribution pages. The page still carries the sentence "we plan to provide a bill of materials, CAD files, circuit diagrams, assembly documentation, and an operation manual." Half of that shipped.
cards.body_zh: Cornell 的 Arachne 靜電紡絲機拿下大學組 Best Hardware，物料清單做得確實出色——三個群組、40 個標價品項，從 $419.00 的 Analog Technologies AHV24V30KVR5MAW 30 kV 高壓模組，到 $0.08 的 M5 螺絲，小計分別是 $681.76／$416.87／$114.72，總計 $1,213.35——製作組裝指南與安全手冊兩份 PDF 也都下載得到。始終沒有出現的是幾何檔：hardware、circuitry、encasement 與 contribution 四個頁面上，沒有任何 STL、STEP、電路圖檔或 ESP32 韌體。頁面上到現在還寫著：「我們計畫提供物料清單、CAD 檔案、電路圖、組裝文件與操作手冊。」兌現的是其中一半。

cards.kicker: Check the link, not the sentence
cards.kicker_zh: 要點連結，不要只看句子
cards.title: An empty Drive folder and a 404 repository
cards.title_zh: 一個空的 Drive 資料夾，和一個 404 的儲存庫
cards.body: Toronto's hardware page links a Google Drive folder named "Bioreactor CAD Files". Opened without a Google account it renders the folder title, lists nothing, and asks you to sign in — so the CAD for its $204 CAD, 96-unit bioreactor array is effectively unavailable, while the firmware next to it is public under Apache-2.0 and the BOM and assembly PDFs both download. HongKong-JSS has the mirror-image failure: its Onshape document is genuinely public (28 parts, full feature tree, view-only) but github.com/hkjssplkchc2026/mercurysense — named on its own wiki as holding the ESP32 firmware, the Hamamatsu C12880 driver and the acquisition instructions — returns 404, and the account has zero public repositories. Only its extraction-unit firmware survived, on a different personal account, with licence "NOASSERTION".
cards.body_zh: Toronto 的硬體頁面連到一個名為「Bioreactor CAD Files」的 Google Drive 資料夾。在沒有 Google 帳號的情況下開啟，只顯示資料夾標題、列不出任何檔案，並要求你登入——所以那台 204 加幣、可達 96 組的生物反應器陣列的 CAD，實際上拿不到，而旁邊的韌體卻以 Apache-2.0 公開，物料清單與組裝說明兩份 PDF 也都下載得到。HongKong-JSS 則是鏡像般的另一種失敗：它的 Onshape 文件確實公開（28 個零件、完整特徵樹、唯讀），但他們自己 wiki 上寫明收著 ESP32 韌體、Hamamatsu C12880 驅動程式與擷取說明的 github.com/hkjssplkchc2026/mercurysense 回應 404，而那個帳號底下一個公開儲存庫也沒有。活下來的只有萃取單元的韌體，放在另一個個人帳號上，授權條款標示為「NOASSERTION」。

cards.kicker: Costs that do not add up
cards.title: The computer is missing from the bill of materials
cards.title_zh: 物料清單裡少了那台電腦
cards.body: NU Boston's FLARE soil chamber leads with "a build cost of as low as $300 vs. $10,000" and then publishes two bills of materials: $499.80 for the entire system and $344.18 for the UV module. Neither total includes the Raspberry Pi 5 that runs the imaging, the Arduino that drives the pumps, the printed and laser-cut enclosure, or the tubing — the module BOM lists a "Raspberry Pi 5 breakout board, $7.50" but not the Pi. So the headline is below both published totals, and both published totals are below the real one. Compare HongKong-JSS, which states outright that its USD 357 core-component build overshot the USD 40 its stakeholders asked for, and TU Darmstadt, which notes that the sensor alone is 83% of its €114.60 oxygen monitor.
cards.body_zh: NU Boston 的 FLARE 土壤模擬艙以「製作成本低至 $300，相對於 $10,000」開場，接著公開了兩份物料清單：整套系統 $499.80、UV 模組 $344.18。兩份總計都沒有包含負責成像的 Raspberry Pi 5、驅動幫浦的 Arduino、列印與雷射切割的機殼，也沒有管路——模組清單裡列了「Raspberry Pi 5 擴展板，$7.50」，卻沒有那台 Pi。於是，標題數字低於兩份公開總計，而兩份公開總計又都低於真實成本。對照之下，HongKong-JSS 直接寫明他們 USD 357 的核心元件成本超出利害關係人要求的 USD 40，TU Darmstadt 也註明光是感測器就佔了那台 €114.60 氧氣監測器的 83%。

cards.title: Eighteen STLs, six manuals — and meshes instead of models
cards.title_zh: 十八個 STL、六本手冊——但給的是網格，不是模型
cards.body: GEMS-Taiwan clears the bar, and it is worth being precise about how narrowly. On the credit side: 18 STL files that download (verified, served as model/stl), six assembly guides of 10 to 16 pages for the bioreactor, both photometers and the light plate, a user manual and brochure, a 6.8 MB hardware notebook covering 23 March to 17 October, print settings recorded next to the files (Bambu Lab X1 Carbon, 0.2 mm, 20% gyroid, PLA Matte with TPU 95A cuvette slots), a published SiO2 OD600 calibration, and CC BY 4.0 on everything. Against: the files are STL meshes, not STEP or parametric source, so a second team can print the photometer but not change its light path; the costs are totals (NT$16,450 in parts; about US$360 for the photometer against roughly US$15,000 for the benchtop instrument it replaces) rather than a priced line-item table; and of the four devices only the reactor rig's sketch.ino is in the MIT digital-twin repo — the photometer and LPA firmware were never released as source. Nobody outside the team has built one.
cards.body_zh: GEMS-Taiwan 過了標準，但值得把「只是剛好過」說清楚。可記上一筆的是：18 個確認可下載的 STL 檔（已驗證，以 model/stl 提供）、生物反應器、兩台光度計與光板各自 10 到 16 頁的六本組裝指南、一本使用手冊與一本型錄、一本涵蓋 3 月 23 日到 10 月 17 日的 6.8 MB 硬體筆記、與檔案並列的列印參數（Bambu Lab X1 Carbon、0.2 mm、20% gyroid 填充、本體 PLA Matte、比色管槽 TPU 95A）、一份公開的 SiO2 OD600 校正文件，以及全部採用 CC BY 4.0。要扣分的是：釋出的是 STL 網格，不是 STEP 也不是參數化原始檔，所以別的隊伍印得出這台光度計，卻改不動它的光路；成本給的是總數（零件 NT$16,450；光度計約 US$360，對照它所取代的約 US$15,000 桌上型儀器），而不是逐項標價的表格；四台裝置裡也只有反應器控制端的 sketch.ino 放進了 MIT 授權的 digital-twin 儲存庫——光度計與 LPA 的韌體從未以原始碼形式釋出。團隊以外，沒有人做過一台。

checklist: Export every part to STEP as well as STL before the wiki freeze. ReLEAF ships 18 STL meshes; a mesh prints but cannot be edited, so nobody can move the photometer's light path. NCKU-Tainan shipped 75 STEP files plus the CadQuery source that generated them.

Publish one itemised bill of materials per device — supplier, part number, quantity, unit price, extended price, subtotal — not a total. Cornell's 40-row table is the model to copy even though Cornell published no CAD; ReLEAF currently gives NT$16,450 and about US$360 with the parts named only inside the assembly guides.

Put all four devices' firmware in the GitLab repo under MIT, not just the reactor rig's sketch.ino. If a file extension is blocked, do what KAUST-KSA did: upload the sketch as .js with a header telling the reader to save it as .ino.

Ship each device as one versioned archive — STEP, STL, BOM CSV, firmware, manual, LICENSE — instead of eighteen loose links on a contribution page. HK League's three zips with a per-file print count are the pattern.

Put the licence inside the bundle, not only in a sentence at the bottom of the page. Bist-China's seven STLs are the only hardware files in the cohort with any stars, and nobody may legally use them because there is no licence file.
Never host design files on Google Drive. Toronto's "Bioreactor CAD Files" folder shows a signed-out visitor nothing at all, which is indistinguishable from publishing nothing.

Write a calibration page per device and keep the honest number in it. The SiO2 OD600 calibration and the leaf-sensor +0.47 to +1.71 degC offset over 540 paired readings are exactly right; add the same for the LPA's per-LED output and the Pro-versus-Slim scale difference.

Cost the whole instrument, including the computer. NU Boston's two BOMs both omit the Raspberry Pi that runs the device; the GEMS cost sheet should state explicitly what the NT$16,450 does and does not cover.

Send one device to one outside laboratory, ask them to run something real, and publish their raw data. Lambert-GA is a high-school team and did this twice, at UAB and Georgia Tech — it is the only outside-use evidence in the entire cohort.
Re-check every hardware link a month after the Jamboree. HongKong-JSS's firmware repository was named on the wiki and is now a 404; a single curl would have caught it.
checklist_zh: 在 wiki 凍結之前，把每個零件同時匯出成 STEP 與 STL。ReLEAF 給的是 18 個 STL 網格；網格印得出來，卻改不動，所以沒有人能調整光度計的光路。NCKU-Tainan 給的是 75 個 STEP，外加生成它們的 CadQuery 原始檔。
每台裝置公開一份逐項的物料清單——供應商、料號、數量、單價、小計金額、分組小計——而不是一個總數。Cornell 那張 40 列的表是值得照抄的範本，即使 Cornell 自己連 CAD 都沒放；ReLEAF 目前只給 NT$16,450 和約 US$360，零件名稱則埋在組裝指南裡。
把四台裝置的韌體都以 MIT 授權放進 GitLab 儲存庫，而不是只有反應器控制端的 sketch.ino。如果副檔名被擋，就照 KAUST-KSA 的做法：把韌體以 .js 上傳，並在開頭寫明請讀者另存為 .ino。
每台裝置打包成一個有版本的壓縮檔——STEP、STL、物料清單 CSV、韌體、手冊、LICENSE——而不是在 contribution 頁面上散落十八條連結。HK League 那三個附帶逐檔列印數量的壓縮檔就是範例。
把授權條款放進壓縮檔裡，不要只寫在頁面底部一句話。Bist-China 的七個 STL 是這批隊伍中唯一拿到星星的硬體檔案，但因為沒有授權條款檔，沒有人可以合法使用。
絕對不要把設計檔放在 Google Drive。Toronto 那個「Bioreactor CAD Files」資料夾對未登入的訪客什麼都不顯示，這和完全沒有公開沒有兩樣。
每台裝置寫一頁校正說明，而且把誠實的那個數字留在裡面。SiO2 OD600 校正，以及葉面感測器在 540 組配對讀數中 +0.47 到 +1.71 degC 的偏移，做法完全正確；LPA 的逐顆 LED 輸出、以及 Pro 與 Slim 之間的尺度差異，也該比照辦理。
把整台儀器的成本算進去，包含那台電腦。NU Boston 的兩份物料清單都漏掉了驅動裝置的 Raspberry Pi；GEMS 的成本表也該明講 NT$16,450 涵蓋與不涵蓋什麼。
把一台裝置寄給一間外部實驗室，請他們跑一件真實的實驗，並公開他們的原始資料。Lambert-GA 是一支高中隊伍，而且做了兩次，分別在 UAB 與 Georgia Tech——這是整批隊伍中唯一的外部使用證據。
Jamboree 結束一個月後，把每一條硬體連結重新檢查一遍。HongKong-JSS 的韌體儲存庫在 wiki 上寫得清清楚楚，現在卻是 404；一行 curl 就能抓到。
method: Twenty instruments were graded: the fourteen Best Hardware winners and nominees across all three sections, plus the six Best Measurement and Best Alternative Platform teams that actually built a device (UNILausanne, Princeton, CalPolySLO, SDU-Denmark, McMaster-Canada, Labi-Taiwan). The remaining Measurement and Alternative Platform teams checked — William-and-Mary, XJTLU-China, WageningenUR, CHINAGuangdongShimen, HangzhouFourteenAP, Yucai-SZ, UOttawa, Marburg, BGI-College — released no instrument and are excluded from the base rate; William-and-Mary's hardware page is still an unfilled iGEM template. Each instrument was scored on seven checkable things: a bill of materials naming parts with prices or part numbers; a total cost and whether it is credible; geometry or electrical source files that actually download; firmware with a licence; an assembly guide a non-author could follow; a calibration or validation protocol; and any evidence of outside use. The pass bar was all of files, priced parts, an assembly guide and a validation protocol, plus firmware where the device needs it. Server-rendered wiki pages were read with curl; client-rendered React wikis were read either from their JavaScript bundles or in a browser — and the browser mattered: a stale deployed chunk on Hongwen School's site still contained the team's own unexecuted editorial placeholders where the CAD link should be, while the live page serves a working 8.56 MB STEP file, so bundle evidence was always confirmed in the browser before being treated as a finding. Every claimed download was fetched and its HTTP status, content type and byte size recorded; Google Drive and Onshape links were opened signed-out. Repositories were queried through the GitLab and GitHub APIs for file tree, licence, stars, forks and last activity. What could not be checked: the contents of bill-of-materials and assembly PDFs, because no PDF text extractor was available in this environment — those files were verified to exist, download and carry the right media type, and their line items were only quoted where the wiki page itself reproduces them. Nor can a link check tell you whether a device reads true, whether an assembly guide is actually followable, or whether anyone has quietly built one; zero stars and zero forks mean no public signal, not certainly no users.
method_zh: 共評分 20 台儀器：三個組別全部 14 支 Best Hardware 冠軍與入圍隊伍，加上 Best Measurement 與 Best Alternative Platform 中真的做出裝置的 6 支隊伍（UNILausanne、Princeton、CalPolySLO、SDU-Denmark、McMaster-Canada、Labi-Taiwan）。其餘被檢查過的 Measurement 與 Alternative Platform 隊伍——William-and-Mary、XJTLU-China、WageningenUR、CHINAGuangdongShimen、HangzhouFourteenAP、Yucai-SZ、UOttawa、Marburg、BGI-College——沒有釋出儀器，因此不計入比率；其中 William-and-Mary 的 hardware 頁面到現在仍是未填寫的 iGEM 範本。每台儀器就七件可查核的事評分：點名零件並附價格或料號的物料清單；總成本以及這個數字是否可信；真的下載得到的幾何或電路原始檔；附授權條款的韌體；非作者也跟得上的組裝指南；校正或驗證流程；以及任何外部使用的證據。通過門檻是：檔案、標價零件、組裝指南與驗證流程四者齊備，裝置若需要韌體則韌體也要有。伺服器端算繪的 wiki 頁面以 curl 讀取；用戶端算繪的 React wiki 則從其 JavaScript bundle 或直接在瀏覽器中讀取——而瀏覽器這一步很關鍵：Hongwen School 網站上一塊過時的已部署 bundle 裡，CAD 連結的位置仍留著團隊自己未執行的編輯備註，但實際上線的頁面提供的是一個可用的 8.56 MB STEP 檔，因此所有 bundle 證據在被當成結論之前，都先在瀏覽器中確認過。每一個宣稱可下載的檔案都實際抓取過，並記下 HTTP 狀態碼、內容型態與位元組大小；Google Drive 與 Onshape 連結都在未登入狀態下開啟。儲存庫則透過 GitLab 與 GitHub API 查詢檔案樹、授權條款、星星數、分支數與最後活動時間。查不到的部分：物料清單與組裝指南 PDF 的內文，因為這個環境沒有可用的 PDF 文字擷取工具——這些檔案只確認了存在、可下載、媒體型態正確，其中的品項只有在 wiki 頁面本身也列出時才被引用。此外，連結檢查也無法告訴你一台裝置讀數是否準確、一本組裝指南是否真的跟得上，或是否有人默默做過一台；零顆星與零個分支代表的是沒有公開訊號，不等於確定沒有使用者。
